mission_02: GPU memory optimization is critical for training large models. Three key techniques are: (1) Memory management with allocation tracking and fragmentation monitoring, (2) Gradient checkpointing that trades compute for memory by selectively saving activations and recomputing others during backpropagation, and (3) Mixed precision training that uses FP16 for activations and gradients while maintaining FP32 master weights for numerical stability. Gradient checkpointing reduces peak memory from O(n) to O(sqrt(n)) by checkpointing every sqrt(n) layers. Mixed precision halves activation and gradient memory while keeping optimizer states in FP32. In this mission, you implement a GPU memory manager with allocation tracking, gradient checkpointing with configurable intervals, and mixed precision memory savings calculation.
